claim.statement: On 1 May 2026, HRANA reported two family-repression cases around execution grief and body retrieval: Akram and Azam Daneshvarkar, sisters of executed Akbar Daneshvarkar, were held in Qarchak after repeatedly seeking his body, while Masoumeh Azhini, sister of a 1988 execution victim, had been incommunicado for 28 days after arrest near Gorgan.
claim.subject: relatives of executed political prisoners
claim.object: post-execution family repression and incommunicado detention

evidence.summary: HRANA says Akram and Azam Daneshvarkar were arrested on 18 April, held for two weeks, transferred to Qarchak, and had repeatedly gone to Qezel-Hesar, forensic medicine, and judiciary offices to receive Akbar Daneshvarkar's body.
HRANA says 63-year-old Masoumeh Azhini, sister of 1988 execution victim Mahmoud Azhini, had been detained for 28 days with family inquiries unanswered.

information_depth.rationale: HRANA provides named relatives, custody locations/status, dates, and charges for one case, but official confirmation and family/lawyer primary documents were not found in this pass.

assessment.uncertainty: Follow for release, charges, Qarchak conditions, family confirmation, and whether body-withholding disputes spread to other execution files.

claim.statement: The v29 xPool anti-execution sample emitted 160 Persian items since 28 April and showed loud anti-execution discourse, but the visible layer remained mostly named-case, prison, family, and opposition-X amplification: top-level keyword counts were execution 160, prison 57, family 23, student-worker 27, street/action 14, named cases 87, and diaspora 3, with no clean independently verified organic in-country mass workplace, student, or street cluster.
claim.subject: Persian X anti-execution discourse
claim.object: prison-family-opposition-X heavy rather than verified mass offline mobilization

evidence.summary: The saved dataset contains 160 emitted Persian X items for anti-execution terms plus family, student, worker, prison, and named-case terms.

The notes record bounded keyword counts and manual inspection: dense Sasan/PMOI/opposition amplification, family-arrest chatter, some May Day worker co-framing, and no clean verified organic mass cluster.

information_depth.rationale: Counts are reproducible for the saved bounded sample, but xPool is not representative and is biased by blackout, organized amplification, and keyword choice.

claim.statement: On 30 April 2026, Judiciary head Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei publicly reinforced the no-leniency execution line, framing rapid and exact punishment of enemy foot soldiers as a public demand and dismissing foreign pressure against executions.
claim.subject: Iranian Judiciary leadership
claim.object: rapid punishment and no-leniency framing for security-case executions

evidence.summary: Mehr reported Ejei's line that rapid, exact, and fair punishment of enemy foot soldiers is a rightful public demand.
The existing AsrIran source in KNB carries the same 30 April judiciary no-leniency framing.
The notes record that VOA and UN-context searches framed the statement as rejecting international calls for restraint.

information_depth.rationale: The line is an official judiciary/media signal repeated across domestic outlets and consistent with earlier KNB execution-deterrence rows.

claim.statement: Follow-up searches on 2 May 2026 did not find confirmed executions of Naser Bakerzadeh, Mehrab Abdollahzadeh, or Yaghoub Karimpour after their late-April transfer from Orumiyeh Prison to unknown locations; the open status remains imminent-risk/unknown rather than resolved.
claim.subject: three Orumiyeh death-row political prisoners

evidence.summary: The notes record name-based Orumiyeh follow-up searches that surfaced transfer warnings but no confirmed executions by 2 May.
IranWire repeated the transfer-to-unknown-location warning for the same three prisoners.
The existing KHRN source originally reported the late-April transfer and imminent-risk status.

information_depth.rationale: This is bounded negative evidence from current searches, not proof of safety; executions can be delayed, hidden, or reported later.

assessment.uncertainty: Requires continued monitoring of KHRN, HRANA, IranWire, family/lawyer statements, and judiciary announcements.

synthesis.title: Cracks in the Islamic Republic, v29 - anti-execution stays prison/family-heavy
synthesis.summary: The twenty-ninth pass does not overturn v19/v26; it sharpens the anti-execution mobilization question. Judiciary leadership is still publicly signaling no leniency, with Ejei casting rapid punishment of enemy foot soldiers as a public demand and dismissing foreign pressure. Sasan Azadvar, Orumiyeh, Tehran Branch 26, and Shiraz/Marvdasht remain the named-case spine. Searches did not find confirmed executions of the three Orumiyeh prisoners by 2 May, so that file remains imminent-risk rather than resolved. The main new crack is family repression: HRANA reports Akram and Azam Daneshvarkar in Qarchak after trying to retrieve Akbar Daneshvarkar's body, and Masoumeh Azhini incommunicado after a Gorgan arrest. xPool shows a loud anti-execution layer, but the visible discourse is still mostly named-case, prison, family, and opposition-X amplification, with some May Day worker co-framing and no clean verified organic workplace, student, or street cluster. Net: executions are not producing silence; they are producing martyr/family amplification. But under blackout and repression, visible anti-execution mobilization has not yet escaped the prison-family-X channel in a verified way.
synthesis.limitations: The family-repression cases rely on HRANA until direct family/lawyer or official records are found. xPool is discourse evidence only and is especially vulnerable to organized amplification. Negative evidence on Orumiyeh is search-bounded and cannot be treated as safety. The next decisive signals are week 119 campaign text, transfer/execution confirmation, releases or charges for family members, and source-near workplace/student/family actions.

information_depth.rationale: The pass combines domestic Persian rights reporting, official judiciary reporting, a saved xPool sample, direct follow-up on open Orumiyeh names, and existing KNB execution rows.

operations.rationale: Family arrests after body-retrieval efforts show anti-execution fallout crossing from prison execution files into family/dadkhahi networks.
The bounded xPool sample directly tests whether the anti-execution campaign is escaping prison/diaspora/X channels into broader mobilization.
The official no-leniency line is a direct input into whether deterrent repression escalates or cracks under pressure.
The 30 April Ejei statement is a current official continuation of the earlier judiciary execution-deterrence framing.
The negative follow-up narrows the Orumiyeh status to still-imminent/unknown rather than confirmed execution by this pass.
